title: Two near-simultaneous weigh-in submits (MorningCheckin + Progress Weight tab) for today create duplicate body_weight_entries rows
setup: Test athlete, tagged rows only (OVN-body-r1-01). Ensure no body_weight_entries row exists for today first (query + delete any if present, since this races the select-then-branch upsert).
steps: 1. Open /today (renders MorningCheckin inline check-in with its own Weigh-in field) in one page/tab. 2. Open /fuel?tab=body (Progress Weight tab) in a second page/tab on the same browser context. 3. Type weight '181' with note 'OVN-body-r1-01' into the Weight tab's Weight+Notes fields (do not submit yet). 4. Type '182' into MorningCheckin's Weigh-in field. 5. Fire both submits back-to-back (Weight tab 'Log' button, then MorningCheckin 'Check In') with under ~200ms between clicks, before either request's isPending has re-rendered the other component.
expected: Exactly one body_weight_entries row for today (an update wins, or a clear conflict signal) — the Weight tab's note field ('OVN-body-r1-01') should be traceable to whichever value 'won', and there should be no silent duplicate.
serializeReason: writes the shared account's 'today' body_weight_entries row and reads/deletes any pre-existing one; must not overlap any other case that logs a weight for today.
risk: src/hooks/useWeighIn.js:105-121 — useLogWeight does `db.entities.BodyWeightEntry.filter({created_by,recorded_date})` then branches create/update; body_weight_entries has no unique constraint on (created_by, recorded_date) (supabase/migrations/00000000000000_remote_schema.sql:210-220). Two calls issued close enough together can both read zero existing rows and both create, producing two rows for the same date — code comment at useWeighIn.js:99-104 explicitly names this exact failure mode as the reason the check exists, just not proofed against concurrent tabs.

title: Progress Weight tab has no bounds check on the weight input, unlike the dashboard weigh-in prompt
setup: Test athlete, tagged via Notes field (OVN-body-r1-02). Athlete's weight_unit is lbs.
steps: 1. Open /fuel?tab=body (Weight tab). 2. Type '1810' into the Weight field, 'OVN-body-r1-02' into Notes. 3. Tap 'Log'.
expected: Either the save is rejected/confirmed (matching WeighInPrompt.jsx's BOUNDS=[50,700] lbs behavior, which shows the parsed value back and asks to double-check) or at minimum a sanity warning, since 1810 lbs is a transposed-digit typo, not a reading.
serializeReason: writes today's body_weight_entries row (or a chosen distinct backfill date to avoid colliding with r1-01 — use e.g. today-3 with the OVN tag) and must not race another weight write for the same date.
risk: src/pages/Progress.jsx:97 — Weight input is `type="number" step="0.1"` with no min/max and no bounds check before `add.mutate()` (:104, disabled only on `!weight || add.isPending`). Contrast src/components/dashboard/WeighInPrompt.jsx:14,96-100 which has exactly this guard (BOUNDS={lbs:[50,700],kg:[25,320]}) one component away from the same write path (both call useLogWeight). Expect this to save silently and skew the weight trend chart / adaptive TDEE.

title: Measurements tab inserts a new row per save instead of upserting-by-date like Weight does — two saves same day = two rows, 'Latest' order unstable
setup: Test athlete, tagged via Notes field (OVN-body-r1-03-am / OVN-body-r1-03-pm).
steps: 1. Open /fuel?tab=body → Measurements tab. 2. Enter Chest=100, Notes='OVN-body-r1-03-am' for today's date, tap 'Save Entry'. 3. Immediately enter Chest=101, Notes='OVN-body-r1-03-pm' for the SAME date, tap 'Save Entry' again. 4. Check the History table and the 'Latest' card.
expected: Either the second save updates the same day's entry (consistent with how Weight logging behaves for a re-logged date) or, if two-per-day is intentional, the 'Latest' card deterministically shows the most recently saved one.
serializeReason: writes two rows to the shared account for the same date; both steps must run back-to-back without another case's measurements write landing in between.
risk: src/pages/Progress.jsx:209-222 — `save` always `supabase.from("measurements").insert(payload)`, no existing-row lookup (unlike useLogWeight). measurements has no unique constraint either (remote_schema.sql:507-519). History query is `order("date", {ascending:false}).limit(10)` with no secondary sort (:202) so two same-date rows' relative order is whatever Postgres returns for a tie — 'Latest' (:233, `history[0]`) is not guaranteed to be the most recently saved row. measurements usage.json shows 0/0 — untested by real usage.

expected: One delete happens; the second tap is a harmless no-op OR is disabled/ignored with clear feedback. No crash, no confusing error toast.

A fast double-tap fires the delete mutation twice against an id that no longer exists on the second call.

title: Typing dose '0' when logging a supplement silently falls back to the default dose instead of logging zero
setup: Test athlete, uses the OVN-body-r1-05-supp type from r1-05 if still present (default_dose=5), or create a fresh one 'OVN-body-r1-06-supp' with default_dose=5.
steps: 1. Open /fuel?tab=hydration. 2. In the supplement's dose field, type '0'. 3. Tap 'Log'. 4. Check the created supplement_logs row's dose value.
expected: The logged dose is 0 (the athlete explicitly typed it), or the UI visibly explains why 0 isn't accepted.

risk: src/pages/Supplements.jsx:264-274 — `dose: parseFloat(dose) || type.default_dose` — `parseFloat('0')` is `0`, which is falsy in JS, so `|| type.default_dose` silently substitutes the configured default (5) instead of the explicitly typed 0. An athlete deliberately logging 'skipped my usual dose, took 0' gets the wrong number recorded with no error.

risk: src/hooks/useWeighIn.js:123-126 — `if (syncProfile && profile?.id && dateStr === getTodayString())` — this guard looks correct on read, so this case is mainly a verification/regression-guard rather than an expected bug, but it's the kind of date-comparison logic worth confirming empirically (string equality between dateStr and getTodayString(), no timezone arg passed to either) rather than trusting by inspection alone.
